newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan discounts Liberia letter citing China ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan discounts Liberia letter citing China ties.

text.p: Taiwan on Wednesday renewed its offer of aid to Liberia, dismissing as invalid a senior Liberian official's statement that the war-torn African country no longer recognised the island's Chinese Nationalist government.

Taiwan is attempting to cement ties with Monrovia ahead of May presidential elections there in the face of an intensified challenge from Beijing, which maintains that it has exclusive formal ties with the West African country.
Monrovia recognises both Taipei and Beijing, an anomaly the rivals have tolerated due to political divisions and confusion in Liberia where civil war has raged for seven years.
Major Taiwan news media on Monday received a faxed statement from one of Liberia's warring factions asserting that Monrovia maintained diplomatic ties only with China.
Taiwan's Foreign Ministry rejected the assertion, by Ruth Perry, chairwoman of the State Council of Liberia National Transitional Government.
"The statement was obviously from certain ambitious elements who tried to use our press freedom to disrupt the development of our normal relations with Liberia," it said in a statement.
The ministry said Taiwan's Liberian ties were firm and unaffected by the 1993 establishment of diplomatic relations with Beijing by a Liberian faction headed by Amos Sawyer.
"The unilateral decision...was not supported by all factions and was thus considered ineffective," Taiwan said.
Perry said that barring any change China would remain as Liberia's diplomatic ally and ordered the suspension of Monrovia's Taipei envoy, John Cummings.
"The Council of State is herewith suspending Ambassador Cummings...for time indefinite for ignoring a directive to abandon his mission to Taiwan," Perry said.

Cummings, who presented his credentials to President Lee Teng-hui in February, told Reuters such a decision required unanimous support of all six council members, not just Perry, and that he had not been formally notified.
"I received no notice at all. If there was such a decision, it must be agreed by all six State Council members," he said.
Cummings said he suspected foul play behind the scenes.
"An invisible person is trying to manipulate," he said without further explanation.
Liberia resumed diplomatic ties with Taiwan in 1989 shortly before civil war erupted with military strongman Charles Taylor launching attacks from neighbouring Ivory Coast.
Taylor, who came to Taiwan last week for a four-day visit and pledged support for the island, is seen as a hopeful in Liberia's May presidential elections.
Taipei, in turn, said Taiwan was "willing to provide necessary aid for Liberia after the new government is established following the May 30 presidential elections."

Beijing refuses to recognise any country that recognises Taiwan's exiled Republic of China. The Nationalists fled there in 1949 after losing a civil war on the mainland, and Beijing regards the island as a rebel province that must eventually be brought back into the fold.
Because of Liberia's domestic turmoil, China apparently has been willing to overlook Monrovia's dual recognition practice.
Taipei has diplomatic relations with just 30 states, mostly underdeveloped countries in Africa and Latin America that rely heavily on the wealthy island's generous aid.
Beijing has stepped up pressure to woo allies away from Taiwan, winning a major victory in November when South Africa announced it would drop Taipei in favour of Beijing in 1997.
Taiwan maintains mutual-recognition pacts with three Pacific Island states that formally recognise Beijing -- Fiji, Vanuatu and Papua New Guinea.
